title: OpsPilot: a support agent whose rules are enforced in code
description: OpsPilot is a support-operations agent for a fictional store. An LLM proposes each action; Python code decides risk, approvals and business rules before anything runs.

og.headline: A support agent whose rules are enforced in code

title: How OpsPilot works: retrieval, planning, approval, execution
description: The eleven-step LangGraph flow behind OpsPilot: parallel retrieval from four sources, a cited plan, code validation, human approval, parallel execution and replanning.

og.headline: Eleven steps from request to explained action

title: OpsPilot safety: the model proposes, code enforces
description: The risk rules, approval gate, business preconditions, citation checks and audit log that stop OpsPilot's model from acting outside policy, with a real audit excerpt.

title: OpsPilot evaluation: live scenario results and held-out tests
description: Scenario-by-scenario results for OpsPilot on the live Groq model and in scripted demo mode, with the held-out set, token costs and the free-tier limits that shaped the runs.

title: OpsPilot demo scenarios: 12 prompts and what happened
description: The twelve demo requests, from a simple policy question to a prompt injection, each with the exact prompt, the steps OpsPilot took and the checks it passed.

title: Run OpsPilot locally: setup, demo mode and commands
description: Set up OpsPilot on your machine with a free Groq key: create the environment, seed the data, run the Streamlit app, or try the scripted demo mode without any key.

title: About OpsPilot and its author, Kushagra Pratap Singh
description: Why OpsPilot was built, what it demonstrates about keeping LLM agents inside policy, and how to reach its author, Kushagra Pratap Singh.
